generalfeedback.text:
For each line: find its equation, read solid or dashed, and test a point in \(R\). The point \(({@nd(G[1])@}, {@nd(G[2])@})\), the centre of the triangle, is in \(R\).

  1. Line 1: {@lind(S[1][1], S[1][2], S[1][3])@}, drawn [[if test="strictp(S[1][4])"]]dashed[[else]]solid[[/if]]; \(R\) is on the side where {@ds[1]@}.

  2. Line 2: {@lind(S[2][1], S[2][2], S[2][3])@}, drawn [[if test="strictp(S[2][4])"]]dashed[[else]]solid[[/if]]; \(R\) is on the side where {@ds[2]@}.

  3. Line 3: {@lind(S[3][1], S[3][2], S[3][3])@}, drawn [[if test="strictp(S[3][4])"]]dashed[[else]]solid[[/if]]; \(R\) is on the side where {@ds[3]@}.

Equivalent forms are also right, for example \(y \le 3\) written as \(3 \ge y\).

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: three inequalities that define a region

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Write the three inequalities that define a clear triangular region on a graph with the unwanted sides shaded.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 1 (Graphing inequalities), Section D, question D7 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new regions with a vertical, a horizontal and a sloping boundary, the unwanted sides shaded.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).
